chunks: And from him, from Abu Ja'far, from his father, from Ahmad ibn al-Nadhr, from Amr ibn Shimir, from Jabir, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:

The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: "God said: 'O son of Adam, remember Me for one hour after the dawn prayer and remember Me for one hour after the afternoon prayer; I will suffice you against whatever concerns you.'

key_terms.أَكْفِكَ: I will suffice you / protect you from
key_terms.سَاعَةً: For an hour (a period of time)
key_terms.مَا أَهَمَّكَ: Whatever concerns you / what weighs on your mind

ai.seo_question: What is the benefit of remembering God after the morning and afternoon prayers according to this hadith?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this hadith qudsi emphasizes the transformative power of consistent dhikr during the post-fajr and post-asr intervals, periods traditionally associated with the transition of spiritual light. Shia scholars highlight this as a practical method for achieving divine sufficiency (kifayah) from worldly anxieties, linking the discipline of time with the purification of the heart.
